system_note: What was billed: Principal diagnosis position 1 is L03.119 (Cellulitis of unspecified part of limb). The claim also lists R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock, MCC), J96.01 (acute respiratory failure with hypoxia, MCC), J80 (ARDS, POA=N), and I63.9 (cerebral infarction, MCC) among other codes. What the record shows: the admitting History & Physical documents the patient as admitted with severe diabetic ketoacidosis complicated by necrotizing fasciitis of the right thigh and "septic shock" (History & Physical (Admitting), History & Physical, p. 810). Deep tissue cultures subsequently grew Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (Discharge / Transfer Summary, Discharge / Transfer Summary, pp. 964-965). The patient was intubated for respiratory failure on admission (Procedure Note - Endotracheal Intubation, Procedure Note, p. 390) and later radiographs/notes document bilateral opacities consistent with ARDS (Nephrology Consultation, Nephrology Consultation, p. 142). Governing policy requires that R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock) be reported only as an additional code with an A40.- or A41.- sepsis code as the principal diagnosis (Policy Documents/DRG/Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx, Scope, position 11). The policy also maps Group A Streptococcus to A40.0 when the organism is identified (Policy Documents/DRG/Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx, Validation Criteria › ICD-10-CM Organism-Specific Sepsis Code Selection Guide, position 84). Reasoning and determination: the medical record documents septic shock on admission (H&P) with positive deep tissue cultures for Group A Streptococcus and MRSA (Discharge Summary). Per the policy, R65.21 must be coded in addition to an A40.-/A41.- sepsis principal diagnosis; therefore coding L03.119 (cellulitis unspecified) as the principal diagnosis is sequencing-inappropriate and does not reflect the condition that occasioned the admission (sepsis/septic shock from necrotizing fasciitis). Additionally, I63.9 (cerebral infarction) is billed as an MCC but there is no neurology consult, stroke imaging, or documentation of an acute infarct in the retrieved chart excerpts to support that code in this admission - I63.9 appears unsupported in the retrieved record and should be removed unless additional supporting imaging/neurology documentation is provided. There is also a duplicate/overlap in the cellulitis coding: L03.119 (unspecified limb) and L03.116 (cellulitis of right lower limb) are both present; the specific code (L03.116) is the correct site-specific diagnosis and the unspecified L03.119 is redundant. Corrections applied in this review (complete corrected lists below): - Principal diagnosis should be an organism-specific sepsis code (A40.0 - sepsis due to Streptococcus pyogenes), with R65.21 retained as an additional code (severe sepsis with septic shock). - Remove L03.119 (unspecified cellulitis) as redundant when L03.116 (cellulitis of right lower limb) is present. - Remove I63.9 (cerebral infarction) due to lack of supporting documentation in the retrieved record. All other diagnoses and procedures reviewed in the record excerpts (acute respiratory failure J96.01, ARDS J80 [POA=N], AKI N17.9, diabetes codes, organism/colonization codes) are supported by the record excerpts cited below and are retained. Key citations used: History & Physical (Admitting) - assessment documenting necrotizing fasciitis and septic shock (History & Physical (Admitting), History & Physical, p. 810); Discharge / Transfer Summary - culture results identifying Group A Strep and MRSA (Discharge / Transfer Summary, Discharge / Transfer Summary, pp. 964-965); Policy requirement that R65.21 be coded with A40.-/A41.- principal (Policy Documents/DRG/Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx, Scope, position 11); policy mapping of Group A Strep to A40.0 (Policy Documents/DRG/Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx, Validation Criteria › ICD-10-CM Organism-Specific Sepsis Code Selection Guide, position 84); intubation procedure note confirming invasive ventilation (Procedure Note - Endotracheal Intubation, Procedure Note, p. 390); Nephrology note documenting P/F ratio ~73 and chest radiograph consistent with ARDS (Nephrology Consultation, Nephrology Consultation, p. 142).
rationale_letter: Dear Provider, This letter documents the results of our DRG coding audit for Claim MR_29 (admission 2026-11-10). We reviewed the medical record and the coding assigned for the entire inpatient stay. Finding: Principal diagnosis sequencing error - the submitted principal diagnosis L03.119 (Cellulitis of unspecified part of limb) does not reflect the clinical condition that occasioned admission and is inconsistent with current sepsis coding guidance. Basis for finding: 1) The admitting History & Physical documents the patient was admitted with severe diabetic ketoacidosis complicated by necrotizing fasciitis of the right thigh and "septic shock" (History & Physical (Admitting), History & Physical, p. 810). 2) Deep tissue cultures subsequently grew Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (Discharge / Transfer Summary, Discharge / Transfer Summary, pp. 964-965), satisfying the policy pathway for organism-identified sepsis. 3) The applicable sepsis policy requires that R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock) be reported only as an additional diagnosis accompanying an organism-specific sepsis code (A40.- or A41.-) in principal position (Policy Documents/DRG/Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx, Scope, position 11). The policy further maps Group A Streptococcus to A40.0 (sepsis due to Streptococcus pyogenes) when the organism is identified (Policy Documents/DRG/Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx, Validation Criteria › ICD-10-CM Organism-Specific Sepsis Code Selection Guide, position 84). Correction applied: We recommend sequencing the principal diagnosis as A40.0 (sepsis due to Streptococcus pyogenes), with R65.21 reported as an additional diagnosis (severe sepsis with septic shock). We also identified the following coding corrections based on the record reviewed: - Remove L03.119 (Cellulitis, unspecified limb) as redundant because L03.116 (Cellulitis of right lower limb) documents the specific site. - Remove I63.9 (Cerebral infarction, unspecified) - no neurology note, stroke imaging, or documentation of an acute ischemic infarct was found in the retrieved chart excerpts to support this code. The remainder of the coded diagnoses and procedures (including J96.01 acute respiratory failure with hypoxia, J80 ARDS [POA=N], N17.9 AKI, diabetes and complication codes, and the listed operative and ventilation procedures) are supported in the record excerpts. If you disagree with the recommended principal diagnosis selection (A40.0) or the removal of I63.9, please provide the specific clinical documentation (physician note, neurology consult, or imaging report) that attributes the sepsis to a different organism or that documents an acute cerebral infarction during this admission. Sincerely, Clinical Claims Audit Team

Requires emergent surgical debridement, aggressive metabolic resuscitation, and multi-organism antimicrobial coverage.
